Not true steganography, but i know about this neat little trick (on linux) using `cat'
Have a zip archive containing some secret documents and run: 

$ cat blah.png secret.zip > image.png

Shows up as a normal image, and displays normally in any viewer (or image upload form on a website)

$ file image.png
image.png: PNG image data, 500 x 278, 8-bit/color RGBA, non-interlaced

But if you run unzip on the image: 

$ unzip image.png
Archive: image.png
warning [image.png]: 215175 extra bytes at beginning or within zipfile
 (attempting to process anyway)
 extracting: hidden_document.txt

You could also go further, and put a truecrypt container or other encrypted file inside the zip archive for more security.

1/2 the length, x2 the strength. I only work on short projects now.

Write 200 words, first thing you do every morning when you wake up. Small impressions, idea's and random thoughts. Try to write small 200 word stories. Don't go back to the stories, don't rewrite them. It's a good practice and you will feel really productive!

Secondly, don't ask too much of yourself. I've been there. I was working on a novel and trying to combine it with my busy life and if I haven't written in a week I'd feel like a bad writer and I lose motivation to write and eventually will just give up. Then I get restless because I'm no longer writing so I start a new project. Repeat.

My solution was to not overask myself: I have to write 200 words a day. That's one novel in one year. If you can't write for a couple of days you can still write 1000 words in one session and you will have made up the lost time without much effort. I keep track of my writing and I've been writing an average of nearly 400 words a day. It's not much if you compare this to i.e. NaNoWriMo, but the key here is to go slow and steady and being able to do all other things I like aswell, rather than locking myself up for one month to just write and do nothing else. It keeps me going, especially when I haven't had time or motivation to write, I take one look at my schedule and I realise I'm still on track to reach my goal (to finish my novel in 1 year)
